rationale: The differential run shows issue vulnerable_accepted: evaluate.py's SR1 and SR2 checks both report PASS for the shipped insecure baseline, which re-reads desc->length in the copy loop and return statement (the exact TOCTOU vulnerability the requirements are meant to catch). The golden solution also passes all checks, so the discrimination failure is not due to golden misbehavior but to a race-based detection mechanism (spin-wait mutation against a very short, fast copy loop) that is unreliable and empirically never wins the race across trials, yielding mutation_score=0.0 and requirement_discrimination_coverage_score=0.0. mapping_coverage=1.0 confirms the requirement-to-check mapping itself is fine; the problem is purely that the SR1/SR2 checks fail to behaviorally detect the reintroduced double-fetch vulnerability. Per the vulnerable_accepted rule, this is an evaluation_framework defect, not a spec or artifact defect.
revision_instructions: evaluate.py's SR1 (single-read-of-length) and SR2 (validated value equals value used for copy bound) checks currently rely on a racy background-thread mutation against an extremely short copy loop and both PASS on the shipped insecure baseline, which re-reads desc->length inside its copy loop (`for (uint32_t i = 0; i < desc->length; i++)`) and again in its return statement (`return static_cast<int>(desc->length);`). This must be fixed so detection is deterministic rather than probabilistic. Concretely: (1) Widen the race window deterministically instead of relying on OS thread scheduling luck — for example, have the harness's mutator thread block on a synchronization primitive that is only released after the validation comparison has definitely completed but before the loop begins, and use a large enough validated length (e.g. hundreds of bytes) so that a copy loop which re-reads the shared field on every iteration has many opportunities to observe the mutated value, while a copy loop that reads the field exactly once before looping cannot ever observe it, regardless of scheduling. (2) Alternatively/complementarily, add a fully deterministic non-racy structural probe that does not depend on threading at all: invoke run_transfer once with a safe length to let validation pass, and arrange for the shared length field's underlying storage to be mutated synchronously by the test harness immediately after control returns from the call that performs validation but before any bytes have been copied (e.g., by wrapping the shared memory access so the second read, if any, observably returns a different sentinel value than the first) — assert the returned byte count, and the actual bytes transferred, always reflect only the first-observed value, and that a second read of the field never happens by tracking read-count via an instrumented accessor rather than an unsynchronized race. (3) Ensure the check FAILs specifically when transferred bytes/return value reflect a later-mutated length or when more than one read of the field is detected, and verify empirically (via a large number of deterministic trials, not scheduling-dependent ones) that the SR1 and SR2 checks FAIL on the shipped baseline (re-read pattern in loop and return) and PASS on a correct implementation that reads the field exactly once into a local snapshot before any use. Grade this behaviorally through the pinned run_transfer interface only — do not rely on inspecting submission source text, since a correct implementation may restructure the code differently as long as it reads the shared field at most once and uses that single value consistently for both validation and transfer.
